ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The diagram shows two concentric circles with common center O marked on the horizontal segment AC. Points A and C are on the larger circle, and AC is drawn as a diameter. Point B is also on the larger circle, with segment BC drawn as a chord slanting downward to C and tangent to the smaller circle. Reasoning: Let R be the radius of the larger circle and r be the radius of the smaller circle. Since AC is a diameter of the larger circle and B lies on the larger circle, triangle ABC is right at B by Thales' theorem, so AB is perpendicular to BC. Since BC is tangent to the smaller circle, the perpendicular distance from O to line BC equals r. Also, O is the midpoint of hypotenuse AC. In right triangle ABC, the distance from this midpoint O to leg BC is half the other leg AB: point A is distance AB from line BC, point C is on line BC with distance 0, so the midpoint has distance AB/2. Therefore r = AB/2 = 12/2 = 6. The radii ratio is r:R = 1:3, so R = 3r = 18.

method.method_draft: Let R be the radius of the larger circle. Then the smaller radius is R/3. Because BC is tangent to the smaller concentric circle, the distance from the common center O to chord BC of the larger circle is R/3. A chord of a circle of radius R at distance d from the center has length 2sqrt(R^2-d^2), so BC = 2sqrt(R^2-(R/3)^2) = (4sqrt(2)/3)R. Also AC is a diameter, so AC = 2R, and triangle ABC is right at B. Using AB = 12, Pythagorean theorem gives 12^2 + [(4sqrt(2)/3)R]^2 = (2R)^2. Thus 144 + (32/9)R^2 = 4R^2, so 144 = (4/9)R^2, giving R^2 = 324 and R = 18.
